events.title: Chrome for Android released
events.summary: Google released Chrome for Android on June 27, 2012 — bringing the WebKit engine and Chrome sync to the world's dominant mobile OS.
events.about: Chrome for Android made mobile browsing a first-class Google product: tab sync with desktop, V8 performance, and later dominance on Android phones. It shipped on WebKit (Google forked Blink from WebKit in April 2013) and extended the Chrome ecosystem beyond desktops.

narrative.whyChosen: Mobile Chrome put Google's browser on the platform that would define the next decade of web usage.
narrative.whyImportant: It made Chrome the default mental model for mobile browsing outside Apple's walled garden.
narrative.problemSolved: Android's stock browser lagged desktop Chrome in speed, sync, and developer tools.

events.title: Coinbase founded
events.summary: Brian Armstrong and Fred Ehrsam founded Coinbase in June 2012 — a regulated on-ramp that let users buy Bitcoin with bank accounts instead of peer-to-peer trades.
events.about: Coinbase wrapped key custody, KYC, and fiat rails in a consumer app — the opposite of cypherpunk self-custody but the path most newcomers took. Its 2021 Nasdaq listing and later spot-ETF custody deals made it the face of mainstream crypto infrastructure in the United States.

narrative.whyChosen: Coinbase became the default fiat gateway for US crypto adoption.
narrative.whyImportant: It proved regulated exchanges could scale without running their own blockchains.
narrative.problemSolved: Buying bitcoin required forum trades and technical wallet setup beyond most users.
